title: Zip, Zip, Zip
novel:
Ted brought a date home. Marshall and Lily happened to be sitting on the bedroom floor, and now they were [[trapped|trap]].

They could not walk out. That would kill the mood. So they became [[hostages|hostage]] in their own flat, [[stranded|stranded]] behind a thin door.

At first it was funny. They [[whispered|whisper]], listened to the [[muffled|muffled]] voices outside, and tried very hard not to [[eavesdrop|eavesdrop]]. Two shadows made one strange [[silhouette|silhouette]] on the wall.

After an hour, hunger arrived. After two, Marshall began to [[starve|starve]]. After three, Lily felt the terrible [[urge|urge]] that no [[blanket|blanket]] can fix: her [[bladder|bladder]] was full, and she had to [[hold it in|hold it in]].

It was pure [[agony|agony]].

They [[tiptoed|tiptoe]] towards the [[doorknob|doorknob]]. A [[floorboard|floorboard]] [[creaked|creak]] loudly. They froze, [[awkwardly|awkwardly]] balanced on one leg each, praying for [[privacy|privacy]] — the very thing they were taking from Ted.

In the end they [[sneaked|sneak]] out at two in the morning and reached the bathroom with enormous [[relief|relief]].

"Love," Marshall said, "means learning to [[endure|endure]] your friends."

trap.en: to keep someone in a place they cannot leave

hostage.en: a person who is kept as a prisoner

stranded.en: left in a place with no way to get out

muffled.en: not clear, because something is in the way

eavesdrop.en: to listen secretly to other people talking

silhouette.en: the dark shape of someone against a light

starve.en: to suffer because you have no food

urge.en: a strong feeling that you must do something now

blanket.en: a thick cover you put over you in bed

bladder.en: the part of your body that holds urine

hold it in.en: to stop yourself from letting something out

tiptoe.en: to walk quietly on the front part of your feet

doorknob.en: the round handle you turn to open a door

floorboard.en: one of the long wooden pieces that make a floor

creak.en: to make a long high noise, like an old door or floor

awkwardly.en: in a way that is not comfortable or graceful

privacy.en: being alone, where others cannot watch or hear you

sneak.en: to move somewhere secretly and quietly

relief.en: the good feeling when something bad or painful stops

endure.en: to suffer something difficult without giving up
